title: Spin-momentum locking of polariton edge states in honeycomb lattices
authors: Andrea Herrero Otermin, Nicola Carlon Zambon, Dheerendra Singh, Neha Bhoria, Rimi Banerjee, Christian Mayer, Simon Betzold, Siddhartha Dam, Monika Emmerling, Sven Höfling, Luis Viña, Subhaskar Mandal, Carlos Antón-Solanas
abstract: Transverse-electric/Transverse-magnetic splitting in dielectric-mirror microcavities introduces an effective spin-orbit coupling for photons. While the bulk states remain linearly polarized, for exponentially localized edge states in a photonic lattice, this coupling induces elliptical polarization whose handedness is locked to the propagation direction, analogous to the transverse spin of evanescent electromagnetic waves. We reveal spin-momentum locking through Stokes polarimetry of zigzag edge states in a honeycomb exciton-polariton lattice. The effect persists in a stretched honeycomb supporting a photonic bandgap, where spin-polarized carrier injection enables selective lasing of either chiral edge states. Our results provide a route toward ultrafast spin-controlled unidirectional propagation in polariton systems without external magnetic fields.
summary: This research demonstrates spin-momentum locking of polariton edge states within honeycomb lattices using semiconductor microcavities. By exploiting the effective spin-orbit coupling inherent to these photonic structures, the authors show that the polarization handedness locks to the direction of propagation. Crucially, they achieve all-optical control by inducing directional lasing whose preferred direction can be switched simply by changing the circular polarization of the pump light.
main_problem: The research aims to demonstrate spin-momentum locking (SML) of polariton edge states and establish an all-optical method for controlling the direction of propagation in these systems without external magnetic fields.
main_result: SML is experimentally confirmed in zigzag edge states, showing that their polarization handedness locks to the propagation direction. Furthermore, spin-selective gain allows for switching the lasing direction purely by changing the pump helicity.
method: The study combines experimental measurements using full Stokes polarimetry and $\mu$-photoluminescence with theoretical modeling based on an effective TE-TM Hamiltonian derived from microcavity physics.
model_or_system: The physical system is excitonic-polariton honeycomb lattices realized in GaAs-based semiconductor microcavities, which serve as a photonic analogue of graphene. The mechanism relies on the effective spin-orbit coupling induced by TE/TM splitting in dielectric-mirror cavities.
key_observables: Elliptical polarization handedness (circular polarization $S_3$) that reverses sign upon momentum reversal ($S_3(k_x) = -S_3(-k_x)$), and spin-selective lasing emission based on pump helicity ($\sigma^+$ vs $\sigma^-$).
important_parameters: The system operates in the polariton regime, utilizing gap opening via stretched lattices to spectrally isolate edge modes from the bulk continuum.
main_assumptions: The SML effect is attributed intrinsically to the evanescent nature of the edge states and the photonic SOC, distinguishing it from previous strain-induced effects.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate SEM images of zigzag edge states (ZES), polarization maps showing opposite handedness for counter-propagating ZES in both regular and stretched lattices, and power-dependent emission confirming spin-selective lasing above threshold.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the theoretical basis using the TE-TM Hamiltonian to predict SML. It then presents experimental verification of this locking in a normal honeycomb lattice via polarization measurements. Finally, it enhances control by fabricating a stretched lattice to open a gap and demonstrate all-optical switching of directional lasing based on pump helicity.
why_interesting: This work bridges concepts from topological physics (edge states), condensed matter magnetism/spintronics (spin-momentum locking), and quantum optics (polaritons). The ability to achieve spin control purely optically in a solid-state cavity platform is highly relevant for developing novel quantum light sources or information carriers.

Spin-momentum entanglement.note: The main result of spin-momentum locking (SML) in polariton edge states—where polarization handedness locks to the propagation direction ($S_3(k_x) = -S_3(-k_x)$)—is a direct demonstration of entanglement between internal (spin/polarization) and external (momentum) degrees of freedom.

Spintronics.note: The study involves polariton physics in semiconductor microcavities, which is an optical system exhibiting spin-orbit coupling effects analogous to those studied in spintronics, particularly through the concept of mode-selective gain and polarization control.
